query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident (email, database, vpn, etc.) is knowable at intake and plausibly correlates with how long resolution takes; it lies outside the focus and carries genuine signal.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The nature of the failure (connection failure vs service outage vs crash) is a diagnostic attribute available early and different modes tend to have different resolution durations. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Breadth of impact (individual user vs department-wide vs server-side) plausibly drives effort and time to resolve; it is an independent characteristic, not a restatement of resolution_time.

per_column.name: assignment_lag
per_column.rationale: A boolean about whether assignment was delayed is derived from timestamps within the incident lifecycle and is a temporal component overlapping the resolution interval; delay-in-assignment is effectively part of the elapsed time, so it leaks/restates the outcome duration.

per_column.name: assigned_equals_closed_by
per_column.rationale: Whether the assignee equals the closer is only knowable once the incident is closed (closed_by is populated at closure), i.e., after the outcome. Post-hoc information constitutes leakage.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Whether the caller is a named end-user vs an ITIL/technical user is known at intake and may correlate with issue complexity and handling speed. Legitimate outside predictor.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Identity of the assigned agent is available once assigned (prior to resolution) and different agents/workloads plausibly carry predictive signal about resolution speed. It is not a function of resolution_time itself.

judge.rationale: Five of the seven added columns are legitimate, pre-outcome predictors: semantic characterizations of the incident (incident_category, failure_mode, scope_indicator) derived from short_description add real signal beyond the raw priority/category fields, and caller_type and assigned_agent contribute additional outside variance. Two columns leak: assignment_lag is a temporal component of the resolution interval, and assigned_equals_closed_by depends on closure information available only after the outcome. As a set the predictors give moderate-to-good genuine leverage for modeling resolution_time, discounted by the two leaking columns.
